result.title: Simplify, Agree, Distill: Label-Free Self-Distillation with Stepping Stones
result.summary: Can a language model teach itself to reason without labels? On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) uses the model as its own teacher, but strengthens that teacher with a ground-truth solution. The natural label-free substitute, voting over the model's attempts, fails precisely on hard problems: attempts disagree, and their most common answer is often wrong. We propose STONE, a label-free alternative that moves agreement to easier related problems. The model writes these stepping stones, keeps those it solves consistently, and shows the teacher their worked solutions, with final answers removed; the student sees only the original problem. No step reads a label, and inference needs no extra context or model calls. Across five math benchmarks, the proposed method achieves the highest average accuracy for Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B in thinking mode. Without thinking mode, it gains 13.2 and 22.7 points, 2.5 and 2.7 times the gains of OPSD with ground-truth solutions.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 STONE：无标签自蒸馏框架，让模型自行改写生成更简单的「踏脚石」问题，只保留能稳定解出的那些，再将其解答（删去最终答案）作为教师上下文，学生仍只看到原题。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心是把一致性筛选与去除答案的示例性解答用作训练监督，而非从答案投票取标签；这一「无标签构造可信过程监督」的思路可供核查 LVR 轨迹训练与监督分配，但论文为纯文本且不涉及视觉或 latent 推理状态。
